policy_statement.policy_description: Florida filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "Florida filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state). Florida has physical presence nexus when corporation: (1) Owns or leases real property in FL, (2) Maintains employees or agents in FL, (3) Has an office or place of business in FL. Reference: FL Statute § 220.11 (Corporate income tax), FL Form F-1120 (Florida Corporate Income Tax Return), FL Department of Revenue Rule 12C-1.011 (Nexus)"

policy_statement.policy_description: Florida filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair).
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "Florida filing required due to economic nexus (post-Wayfair). Florida economic nexus thresholds (lower than many states): $50,000 or more in gross receipts from FL, OR 200 or more separate transactions in FL. Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018), FL Statute § 220.14 (Apportionment of income), FL Department of Revenue TIP 22C1-02 (Economic Nexus)"

policy_statement.policy_description: No Florida nexus - no filing requirement.
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "No Florida nexus - no filing requirement. Any estimated payments would be refunded."

policy_statement.policy_description: Florida state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "Florida state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income. Additions to federal taxable income: (1) Interest on U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to FL), (2) State income tax refunds included in federal income, (3) IRC § 78 gross-up for deemed paid foreign tax credit, (4) Addback of certain federal deductions not allowed by FL. Subtractions from federal taxable income: (1) Interest on municipal bonds from other states (if taxable federally), (2) Certain dividend income qualifying for FL exemption, (3) Florida net operating loss deduction (separate from federal NOL), (4) Excess qualified production activities income deduction. Reference: FL Form F-1120 Schedule I (Adjustments to Federal Taxable Income), FL Statute § 220.13 (Computation of Florida taxable income), FL Department of Revenue Form F-1120 Instructions"

policy_statement.policy_description: Florida state corporate income tax calculation
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "Florida state corporate income tax calculation: (1) Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28], (2) Apportioned to FL: × [Apportionment % - single-sales factor], (3) FL additions: + [Additions from Schedule I], (4) FL subtractions: - [Subtractions from Schedule I], (5) FL taxable income: = [Result], (6) FL tax rate: × 5.5% (flat rate), (7) FL income tax: = [Tax before credits], (8) FL credits: - [Credits from Schedule II], (9) FL tax liability: = [Final tax]. Florida has a flat 5.5% corporate income tax rate on Florida taxable income. Available FL credits include: Enterprise zone jobs credit, Research and development credit, Community contribution tax credit, Capital investment tax credit, Renewable energy production credit, Florida Entertainment Industry Financial Incentive. Reference: FL Form F-1120 (Florida Corporate Income Tax Return), FL Statute § 220.11 (Tax rate: 5.5%), FL Statute § 220.13 (Florida taxable income computation), FL Statute § 220.14 (Single-sales factor apportionment), FL Statute § 220.181-.197 (Tax credits)"

policy_statement.policy_description: No Florida nexus - no tax liability.
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "No Florida nexus - no tax liability. Any estimated payments are refunded."

policy_statement.policy_description: No Florida taxable income - no tax liability.
policy_statement.policy_statement_postfix: "No Florida taxable income - no tax liability. Florida allows net operating loss (NOL) carryforwards: (1) NOLs may be carried forward up to 20 years, (2) NOL carryback not allowed under FL law, (3) FL NOL calculated separately from federal NOL. Reference: FL Statute § 220.13(1)(b) (NOL deduction)"
